q: Do kiln start-up oil and raw material dryer fuel count in a cement plant's CBAM figure?
title: Kiln start-up oil in a CBAM figure
short: Yes. Every fuel burnt inside the installation for making clinker and cement counts as a direct emission, including oil or diesel used to light up the kiln after a stop and fuel for raw material or coal dryers. Leaving them out understates the figure and fails a verifier's completeness check.
audience: Cement plants listing fuels for CBAM monitoring

ul: Main kiln and calciner fuels: coal, pet coke, alternative fuels.
Start-up fuel: light diesel oil, furnace oil or HSD.
Dryer and hot gas generator fuel.
Diesel for mobile equipment inside the boundary, if your method includes it.

p: Take quantities from stock and issue registers, not only from purchase invoices, and convert with the fuel's net calorific value and factor.
Start-up fuel is a small share, but verifiers compare fuel registers with purchases. A missing line looks like a control gap.
